blocks.q: The ACK for a sent message is lost after the server persisted it. The client retries, but its code builds a fresh UUID for every attempt. What does the receiver see, and what is the fix?
a_bullets: The server cannot tell the retry from a new message, so it stores a second copy
The receiver sees the same text twice
Fix: create `client_msg_id` once per message and reuse it on every retry
The server then finds the ID, skips the write and returns the stored result
example_code: # bug: new id on every attempt

blocks.q: A channel has 1M members and fan-out on write is used as for 1,024-member groups. What happens for one post, and what do you change?
a_bullets: The message is stored once, but 1M delivery tasks are queued for that single post
Kafka lag and gateway load spike, and most members are offline anyway
Switch to fan-out on read: members pull new posts using their last seen ID
Keep fan-out on write for small groups, where one canonical order is cheap

blocks.q: A teammate proposes one global counter so every message in the system gets a single total order. Why is this a bad design?
a_bullets: It is a single coordination point for about 1.2M msg/s average and ~3M peak
Users only need order inside a conversation, so a global order buys nothing
Fix: a monotonic sequence per `conversation_id`, owned by that conversation's shard
Snowflake-style IDs stay unique and sortable without any coordination

blocks.q: The receiver's phone is off when a message arrives. The session lookup misses. What happens next, and why is the push payload tiny?
a_bullets: The message stays in the recipient's inbox queue and a push job is created
The push goes through APNs or FCM with a small payload and no plaintext, since the content is E2EE
The woken app reconnects and sends `last_seen_message_id`
The server drains the inbox in order and deletes each entry after the client ACKs it

blocks.q: A user opens a chat with 200 unread messages. One design writes a read-receipt row per message. Why is it wrong, and what should be sent instead?
a_bullets: It creates 200 writes and 200 messages back to the sender, and receipts are already ~30% of traffic
Instead, send one receipt carrying `last_read_message_id` for the conversation
Store only `last_delivered_id` and `last_read_id` per user per conversation
In a group, show read only when every member's `last_read_id` has reached the message
